note: More mail ballots returned than transmitted. Often a timing or scope difference: some jurisdictions count transmissions in an earlier reporting period, or report UOCAVA transmissions separately from the domestic total.
Counted plus rejected exceeds returned. Undeliverable and spoiled ballots are reported separately, so they do not explain an excess here.
More UOCAVA ballots returned than transmitted. Ballots transmitted before the reporting window opens are a common explanation.
Counted plus rejected exceeds UOCAVA ballots returned. Note the B18a/B24a renumbering: verify the year's codes before reading much into this one.
Federal write-in absentee ballots counted exceeds those returned.
Provisional ballots counted in full, counted in part, and rejected together exceed those submitted.
Active registrations exceed total registered and eligible voters. States differ in whether the total includes inactive registrants, so compare against reg_inactive before drawing a conclusion.
New valid registrations plus rejected forms exceed forms received. Duplicate and update forms are counted differently across jurisdictions, which routinely produces an excess here.

Participation by mode sums to more than total participation. Mode categories overlap in some states, notably by-mail against all-mail elections, so an excess here often reflects a reporting convention rather than a discrepancy in the count.

Rejection reasons summing past the rejected total. The curated reasons are a subset - the survey also offers Other 1-3, and 2018/2020 offer a missing election-official signature - so they are expected to sum to LESS than the total; exceeding it usually means a jurisdiction counted one ballot under more than one reason, or reported reasons for a wider set of ballots than the total covers.

Provisional rejection reasons summing past the rejected total. The curated reasons exclude Other 1-3, so they are expected to sum to LESS than the total; exceeding it usually means one ballot counted under more than one reason.
